    Garlic Parmesan Chicken Thighs with Beans and Cabbage

    These Garlic Parmesan Chicken Thighs with Beans and Cabbage are a comforting and delicious fall dinner that just so happens to be loaded with nutrients. Thanks to the beans, parmesan, chicken, and yogurt this recipe has plenty of protein and fiber. It is also cooked in one pan for minimal cleanup.

    Each serving has 45 grams of protein and 15 grams of fiber.

    For more yummy chicken thigh recipes try my chipotle chicken thighs, mediterranean chicken thighs or my lemon parmesan chicken thighs.

    Why you'll love this one pot parmesan chicken with cabbage and leeks

    Protein and fiber packed. Chicken thighs, butter beans, and Greek yogurt make this a satisfying meal with plenty of protein and fiber.

    Loaded with seasonal vegetables. Cabbage, parsley and leeks add fall seasonal flavor and plenty of nutrients.

    Easy cleanup. The chicken and vegetables cook in the same skillet making cleanup a breeze.

    Perfect for meal prep. The chicken and bean mixture reheat beautifully, making this a great option for leftovers.

    Ingredients

    • Boneless, skinless chicken thighs
    • Garlic powder
    • Onion powder
    • Smoked paprika
    • Salt

    Substitutions

    • Chicken thighs: Boneless skinless chicken breasts can be used instead of thighs. Just adjust the cooking time as needed to avoid overcooking them.
    • Butter beans: While I do recommend using b
    • Greek yogurt: Any unsweetened yogurt will work but will alter the protein content
    • Parsley: Basil would be a good substitution.
    • Dried rosemary/thyme: feel free to sub in one or more of the other or use an all purpose italian seasoning blend.
    • Cabbage: shredded Brussels Sprouts also work.

    Step-by-Step Instructions for chicken thighs with yogurt sauce

    Mix together the sauce.

    Sear the chicken thighs.

    Cook the veggies.

    Assemble and serve.

    Storage instructions

    You can store the extra chicken thighs in a sealed container in your fridge for up to 4 days.

    Recipe Pro-Tips

    Use an instant-read thermometer and cook the chicken to 175-180°F for perfectly juicy chicken.

    Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before slicing to retain its juices.

    Use a good quality pasture raised chicken for the best tasting and healthiest chicken.

    Use a good quality grass fed yogurt for the best tasting sauce.

    Recipe FAQS

    Can I make this recipe ahead of time?

    Yes, this recipe stores well and is perfect for meal prep.

    Can I use chicken breasts instead of thighs?

    Yes! Boneless, skinless chicken breasts work well in this recipe. Just adjust the cooking time based on their thickness and cook to an internal temperature of 165°F.

    What are the health benefits of cabbage?

    Cabbage is packed with fiber, antioxidants, and essential nutrients like vitamins C and K, which support immune health, digestion, and bone health. It also contains beneficial plant compounds that help reduce inflammation and support overall gut health.

    Garlic Parmesan Chicken Thighs with Beans and Cabbage

    These Garlic Parmesan Chicken Thighs with Beans
    5 from 1 vote
    Print Recipe Pin Recipe
    Prep Time 10 minutes mins
    Cook Time 23 minutes mins
    Course dinner
    Cuisine American, high fiber, high protein
    Servings 4
    Calories 510 kcal

    Equipment

    • 1 skillet
    • mixing bowls
    • garlic press

    Ingredients
      

    Yogurt sauce

    • ½ cup greek yogurt
    • 1-2 tablespoons water optional to thin the sauce, adjust to your thickness preference
    • 1 teaspoon grated parmesan
    • pinch salt adjust to your saltiness preference
    • 2 teaspoons olive oil
    • 1 clove garlic - pressed or grated
    • juice from ½ lemon

    Chicken

    • ~1.2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs 4 thighs total
    • 1 teaspoon salt
    • ¼ teaspoon black pepper
    • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
    • ½ teaspoon onion powder
    • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
    • 1-2 tablespoons avocado oil can use olive oil but avocado oil is better for searing

    Beans and veggies

    • 3 leeks - separated from green, halved and finely sliced
    • 6 cups shredded cabbage from 1 small cabbage or ½ head of a large head of cabbage
    • ½ teaspoon mustard
    • pinch red pepper flakes
    • ½ teaspoon dried rosemary
    • ½ teaspoon dried thyme
    • 6 cloves garlic
    • ⅓ cup finely chopped parsley
    • ¼ cup grated parmesan
    • 2 cans butter beans - DO NOT DRAIN* 13-15 oz size cans or boxes

    Instructions
     

    • Add all yogurt sauce ingredients to a bowl and mix together until combined. Set aside.
    • Pat chicken thighs dry and coat each side in garlic powder, smoked paprika, onion powder, salt and pepper.
    • Heat oil in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add chicken thighs skin side down and sear for 5-6 minutes, until browned. Flip and cook for another 5-6 minutes, until browned on the other side.
      I like to cook my thighs to 175-180 degrees. Chicken thighs taste better when cooked to a higher temp.
      Remove thighs from the pan, leaving in any leftover fat/oil and let rest while you cook the vegetables.
    • Turn off heat and let pan cool for 3 minutes. Then turn heat to medium and add leeks. Cook for 5 minutes.
      Add cabbage, parmesan mustard, garlic, salt, pepper, thyme, rosemary, and parsley to the pan. Cook for 10-15 more minutes, tossing occasionally, until cabbage is broken down and everything is browned.
      Add beans and their liquid to the pan. Toss everything together and cook for 3 minutes, until everything is fragrant and flavorful.
    • Slice chicken thighs.
      Divide out bean/veggie mixture. Top with chicken thigh and then drizzle over sauce.

    Notes

    *This should be ½ cup of liquid. If you forget to drain the beans you can also add broth.
